intro.name: The recitation
intro.text:
At the annual gathering of stories, (Reciter) has been invited to recite a beloved {poem|song|verse|ceremonial teaching|ancestral chronicle}. The text has been repeated for generations. (Reciter) has practiced for weeks and is determined to do it justice.
Unfortunately, the first line comes out wrong.

err1.name: The error
err1.text: (Reciter) replaces a solemn word with a term for animal droppings.

choices.label: Invite the scholars to debate the performance.

err2.name: The error
err2.text: (Reciter) accidentally praises a historical villain instead of a hero.

choices.label: Invite the scholars to debate the performance.

err3.name: The error
err3.text: A forgotten pause changes a blessing into an apparent insult.

choices.label: Invite the scholars to debate the performance.

err4.name: The error
err4.text: A misremembered rhyme makes the ancestors sound like greedy goats.

choices.label: Invite the scholars to debate the performance.

err5.name: The error
err5.text: (Reciter) sings a funeral verse to the melody of a drinking song.

choices.label: Invite the scholars to debate the performance.

err6.name: The error
err6.text: The performance accidentally implies that the village's founders were extraordinarily bad at farming.

choices.label: Invite the scholars to debate the performance.

err7.name: The error
err7.text: (Reciter) repeats an obscure archaic word with a very embarrassing modern meaning.

choices.label: Invite the scholars to debate the performance.

err8.name: The error
err8.text: (Reciter) improvises a verse that sounds like a personal attack on the village's most respected elder.

choices.label: Invite the scholars to debate the performance.

a1.text:
THE NEW SONG:
The crowd bursts into laughter.

a1_more.text: Instead of stopping, (Reciter) finishes the entire verse in the same ridiculous style. By morning, children are singing it everywhere. Within a generation, the comic version has become a beloved festival song, though the original is still preserved by the elders.

a2.text:
THE OFFENSE:
An elder rises and says the performance dishonors the ancestors.

a2_more.text: (Reciter) is mortified. A discussion follows, distinguishing honest mistakes from deliberate mockery. The elder accepts an apology but asks that the original verse be taught accurately.

a3.text:
THE REVELATION:
The mistaken line causes the audience to hear a familiar teaching in a startling new way.

a3_more.text: The Keeper of Verses calls it "an accident of considerable wisdom." The scholars record both versions.

a4.text:
THE LEGEND OF THE GOAT:
(Reciter)'s mispronunciation becomes a story about a legendary goat that supposedly saved the village.

a4_more.text: Nobody remembers who first told it. Years later, a scholar attempts to prove that the goat existed.

b1.text:
THE GRACEFUL RECOVERY:
(Reciter) admits the error, begins again, and performs beautifully.

b1_more.text: The audience applauds the courage to correct a mistake.

b2.text:
THE WORSE APOLOGY:
In apologizing, (Reciter) accidentally repeats the offensive phrase three times, each louder than the last.

b2_more.text: The Keeper of Verses begs (reciter.him/her) to stop speaking. The village remembers the apology more vividly than the original error.

b3.text:
THE HUMILIATION:
(Reciter) flees the stage in tears.

text_only.reason: the reciter leaves the stage, not the village

b3_more.text: A teacher later reminds the crowd that public laughter can wound even when nobody means harm. A few villagers visit (Reciter) and offer encouragement.

text_only.reason: the reciter leaves the stage, not the village

b4.text:
THE COMPASSION:
The elder whose honor was supposedly insulted stands and recites the next line alongside (Reciter).

b4_more.text: Together they finish the poem. The crowd is moved to silence.

c1.text:
THE BRILLIANT INTERPRETATION:
(Reciter) explains that the altered wording was intended to question whether the old heroes were flawless.

c1_more.text: The Keeper of Verses praises the thoughtful reading while noting that the original text should still be accurately identified.

c2.text:
THE DESPERATE EXCUSE:
(Reciter) claims the ancestors spoke entirely in goat metaphors.

c2_more.text: A historian asks for evidence. (Reciter) has none. The audience laughs; (Reciter) admits the mistake.

c3.text:
THE HEATED DISPUTE:
A devotee argues that the verse must never change.

c3_more.text: A scholar insists that reinterpretation keeps traditions alive. The leaders allow both to speak and commission a record of the debate.

c4.text:
THE NEW TRADITION:
The villagers begin performing the solemn original at dawn and the comic reinterpretation at sunset.

d1.text:
THE SCHOLARLY CRITIQUE:
Three scholars produce an exhaustive commentary on the mistaken line.

d1_more.text: It is longer than the original poem. A child asks whether they have all lost their minds.

d2.text:
THE GREAT DISAGREEMENT:
The Keeper of Verses declares the error unforgivable.

d2_more.text: Another scholar calls it a masterpiece. Their argument becomes a yearly public debate that draws enthusiastic crowds.

d3.text:
THE LOST ORIGINAL:
An elder reveals that the supposedly incorrect wording appears in an ancient copy of the verse.

d3_more.text: Nobody knows which version came first. (Reciter) becomes famous for rediscovering a forgotten line entirely by accident.

d4.text:
THE BITTER SATIRIST:
(Reciter) embraces the controversy and writes increasingly outrageous verses mocking village pretensions.

d4_more.text: Some villagers adore the work; others are offended. The leaders protect peaceful criticism while asking (Reciter) not to spread false accusations as fact.

d5.text:
THE LEGACY:
Generations later, children learn both the traditional verse and "(Reciter)'s Version."

d5_more.text: Scholars still argue over its meaning. The original embarrassment has become part of Isola's history.
